summary: This file creates a collapsible code snippet component with optional AI-powered explanations. It supports displaying code from either a string or React children, automatically detects the programming language, and can show line-by-line tooltips or a full summary explanation when that data is available. The component also includes a copy button and uses Prism for syntax highlighting.

explanations.27: These imports load language definitions into Prism so it knows how to highlight code for languages beyond its default bundle. They're imported here unconditionally so the component doesn't depend on other code blocks rendering first.
explanations.54: This function recursively searches through nested React elements to find a className like 'language-xyz' and extract the language name.
explanations.62: The regex looks for a pattern like 'language-' followed by word characters, and extracts just the word part (the [1] index).
explanations.83: This object maps different code file extensions and language names to a standardized variant name used for styling and icon selection.
explanations.150: This object holds metadata for each language variant, including which CSS class to use for the icon styling and which iconify icon ID to display.
explanations.336: This creates a ref that holds a timeout ID number, allowing the component to remember and clear the timer when it unmounts.
explanations.340: The code clears any previously pending timeout before setting a new one, preventing multiple timeouts from stacking up.
explanations.346: This cleanup function runs when the component unmounts and clears any lingering timeout so it doesn't try to update state on an unmounted component.
explanations.352: State tracks which line number (if any) currently has its explanation tooltip open.
explanations.357: This flag starts as false and is set to true only after the component mounts on the client, allowing the code to safely render a Portal into document.body.
explanations.376: This memoized value either gets the grammar for the detected language or falls back to plaintext or clike if the language isn't recognized.
explanations.387: If there's a synthetic last 'line' added by the tokenizer (just containing a newline), it's removed so line numbers stay in sync with the eli5 explanations object.
explanations.399: The tooltip's vertical position is set to the badge's position, but CSS transform will shift it upward; the right value is calculated so the tooltip is right-aligned with the badge.
explanations.416: The scroll listener uses capture phase to catch the scroll event early before it propagates, and passive:true tells the browser it won't call preventDefault().
explanations.462: This callback-style ref assignment updates the badgeRefs object whenever a button mounts or unmounts, storing each button by its line number.
explanations.493: createPortal renders the tooltip into document.body instead of the normal component tree, letting it escape overflow:hidden containers.
explanations.524: useId() generates a unique ID scoped to this component instance, ensuring the aria-controls/aria-labelledby references match even when multiple Eli5SummaryBlocks exist.
explanations.528: The content's max-height is set to either its actual scroll height (when open) or 0px (when closed), creating a smooth collapse animation.
explanations.592: JSON.parse converts the serialized eli5json string (injected at build time) back into a JavaScript object mapping line numbers to explanations.
explanations.606: contentRef.current.scrollHeight gets the actual height of the content even though it may be visually hidden by maxHeight:0, allowing smooth expand/collapse.
explanations.623: split('.') breaks the filename into parts, and pop() gets the last one (the extension); if it doesn't exist or isn't recognized, it defaults to plaintext.
explanations.637: substitutePlainText does string replacements for variable markers like %%name=default%% in plain text code before passing it to Prism.
explanations.651: The code block uses the special line-by-line renderer only when eli5 annotations exist and we have actual code string; otherwise it falls back to the standard CodeBlock.
explanations.663: toLowerCase() normalizes the filename for case-insensitive comparison against docker file name patterns.
explanations.671: The isDockerFile check tests multiple docker-related filenames (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yaml, etc.) because Docker uses several different naming conventions.
explanations.687: If no explicit variant was provided, the variantKey is determined by checking if it's a docker file, docusaurus config, or a known language, with 'none' as fallback.
explanations.699: displayTitle prefers an explicit title, falls back to filename, then to the language name in uppercase, and finally to the generic 'Snippet'.
